stem: A rural hospital without an on-site stroke neurologist activates its telestroke system for a client with suspected acute ischemic stroke. What is the main benefit of this system?

options.A: It gives the local team rapid remote access to stroke expertise and imaging review to support thrombolysis, triage, and transfer decisions when on-site specialists are unavailable.
options.B: It replaces all in-person nursing, emergency, radiology, and follow-up care for the remainder of the hospitalization.
options.C: It is useful mainly in large academic centers and offers little benefit to remote hospitals without local neurologists.
options.D: It should be used only after reperfusion-treatment decisions are complete because telemedicine has little role in acute stroke evaluation.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline states that telestroke bridges gaps in access to stroke expertise, particularly in remote locations. In the emergency setting, telestroke and teleradiology support timely review of brain imaging, thrombolytic decision-making, and triage or transfer for endovascular thrombectomy when appropriate. B overstates telemedicine as a replacement for local hands-on care. C reverses its equity/access purpose. D is incorrect because acute treatment decisions are a central telestroke use.
educational_objective: Use telestroke as a systems-of-care resource that brings remote stroke expertise to hospitals without on-site specialists and supports rapid imaging interpretation, reperfusion decisions, and transfer planning while local clinicians continue hands-on care.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
source_locator: Section 2.8 Telemedicine — Synopsis: telestroke bridges access gaps for remote patients; in acute ED care, teleradiology/telestroke enable timely brain-imaging review, thrombolytic decision-making, and timely treatment. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text: telestroke supports hospitals without on-site neurological expertise and can aid triage/transfer for EVT or allow appropriate local care.
source_claim_supported: Telestroke provides remote specialist consultation and imaging-based decision support for acute stroke, improving access to timely thrombolysis and transfer/triage decisions in hospitals lacking on-site stroke expertise.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: coordinate interdisciplinary and telehealth resources, arrange consultation and transfer, and use systems that improve access to timely care.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — telestroke consultation and transfer coordination
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw technology-definition item into a care-coordination scenario and corrected the blueprint from Safety & Infection Prevention and Control to Management of Care. The final item reflects the 2026 AHA/ASA telestroke role across imaging, thrombolysis, and EVT triage without claiming telemedicine replaces local in-person care.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against Section 2.8 of the 2026 AHA/ASA AIS guideline.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reflects remote expertise, imaging review, reperfusion decisions and transfer triage. B falsely replaces all local care. C denies the principal remote-access benefit. D removes telemedicine from the acute phase where it is specifically valuable.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; rapid remote stroke expertise integrated with local care.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; telemedicine complements rather than replaces bedside care.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; remote/underserved access is a major use case.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; telestroke directly supports acute treatment decisions.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A captures the evidence-supported role without overclaiming that every patient requires transfer or that telemedicine replaces local clinicians.
audit_findings.cueing: All options define the operational role of telestroke in the same setting.
audit_findings.blueprint: Consultation, transfer, and telehealth coordination fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked telestroke versus telephone-only consultation, teleradiology, EVT transfer, and local drip-and-stay models. The answer preserves local clinical responsibility and no second defensible answer remained.
